headlines.full_text: A thousand slogans echoed here - but it could be the end for iconic Delhi protest site Jantar Mantar, an 18th Century site almost synonymous with demonstrations in Delhi, has been denotified as a protest site. What is the point of a protest? To raise your voice against injustice? To draw attention to a cause? Or to make those in power uncomfortable enough to listen? For more than three decades, Indians have tried to do all three in a narrow, tree-lined road near Jantar Mantar, an 18th Century astronomical obervatory in Delhi. But that may now be coming to an end. This week, Delhi Police said Jantar Mantar, located close to parliament, would no longer be a designated protest site. The decision comes months after the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) - not a political party but a collectivewhich began as a joke- led a massive protest there demanding the resignation of federal education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Tens of thousands turned up and Pradhan subsequently resigned. Police barricaded Jantar Mantar soon afterwards, preventing further demonstrations. Last week, an attempt by CJP supporters to march there, this time demanding the resignation of India's election chief,ended in a police crackdown. Protesters have now been directed to three other sites. Two are far from parliament, while the third, the sprawling Ramlila Ground, is often booked months in advance. Unlike Jantar Mantar, which is free, all three charge tens of thousands of rupees a day. Delhi Policesays,externalit acted after the Supreme Court suggested identifying alternative sites with adequate infrastructure. French President Emmanuel Macron has called for "calm and order" after a major day of protests turned into rioting and looting on Saturday, and as some disorder continued in Paris on Sunday. In a national address from the Élysée Palace, he warned those who had taken part not to "escalate", adding: "We all feel anger and shame." Some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for largely peaceful protests against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools. Macron said a distinction must be drawn between the "legitimate demands" of protesters and "those who destroyed, smashed and looted". Police have arrested about 2,400 people, according to France's interior ministry. The French president said "nothing justifies" the "unbridled" violence seen and said those involved would face justice. Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings. On Sunday, looting and clashes with police continued on a smaller scale in parts of the capital and Lyon. Tear gas and stun grenades were fired at hundreds of people in Paris, according to the AFP news agency, and bottles and rocks were again hurled at police. Sunday saw cities across the country confront the impact of what developed into one of the worst bouts of disorder in modern French history. Iranian state media quoted the Guards as saying the vessel, which it described as being "in violation", struck a naval mine south of the strait. The blast, it said, caused an explosion and a fire in the ship's engine room. According to the statement, the tanker was using what the Guards called the "unauthorized southern route" and had switched off its positioning and navigation systems. The report followed an announcement a day earlier by the Guards that two oil tankers had caught fire in the strait, both after hitting mines. Earlier this week, the Guards' naval commander, Admiral Ali Ozmaei, warned that any vessel deactivating its navigation systems would be treated as "hostile". Iran took control of the strait after war broke out against the United States and Israel in late February, choking a shipping route that normally carries about a fifth of the world's oil. headlines.full_text: Trump says suspension of Russia sanctions is to keep peace negotiations going The US president blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect. US President Donald Trump has said his decision to suspend several Russian sanctions is an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table. "I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine," Trump said on his Truth Social messaging platform, adding that he didn't want to "do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table". Trumpblocked numerous sanctions on Russiaon Friday night, two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky deepened. Zelensky told NBC News on Sunday that siding with Russian President Vladimir Putin would be a "historic mistake". Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev has responded to Trump's order by calling it "an important and truly historic moment". He said the sanctions, which were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by the US president in September, would have inflicted "serious damage" on the US and global market. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has described the suspension of the sanctions as a 60-day pause during which their potential impact on the US and global economies would be analysed. In his Truth Social post, Trump also said Zelensky "doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did", adding "he could have made a better deal two years ago than he can now". Zelensky has pushed for an end to fighting, and has repeatedly said that Putin doesn't want peace, since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

headlines.full_text: How reliant is Ukraine on the US-controlled Starlink internet service? Kyiv keeps issuing warnings that the satellite internet system Starlink is being restricted in Ukraine. How dependent is the country on the system, and what would happen if it went down? Few technological systems have played such an important role in thewar in UkraineasStarlink, central to the communications, reconnaissance and drone operations of the Ukrainian armed forces. There are currently widespread concerns thatElon Musk's satellite internet service in Ukraine may be restricted or even switched off. In recent days, Kyiv has repeatedly reported disruptions and restrictions affecting its use. Since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, Ukraine has made extensive use of the satellite internet service, which is operated by the US company SpaceX. With it, military personell can continue to communicate and exchange data, even when infrastructure has been destroyed or cellphone networks are down. According to the Center for Security Studies (CSS) at ETH Zurich, around 50,000 Starlink terminals were in use in Ukraine in 2025. These are the system's specialised receiving and transmitting devices, which enable communications on the battlefield. In this piece, we take a longue durée view of macroeconomics to situate their work within the context of political economy. In many ways, the field has come full circle from the days of John Maynard Keynes and Michal Kalecki (henceforth KK) Economists are products of their times.
